inspiration: Map markers as one small flat glyph per category (sound, light, effect, object, particle, shadow, entity), all in one set of 64x64 SDF images. For Frankendom: one glyph per spawn or loot category, readable at 375 wide.

Icons drawn as signed-distance images: author a simple vector shape, bake it to a distance field, then draw it at any size with a crisp edge. Interface icons are 32x32 and overlay icons 64x64. Useful for the HUD and minimap pins.
Pathing overlays are simple directional glyphs (straight, diagonal, goal), so a walk path reads as a set of arrows. Could show a lock-on or route hint without a full decal.
Localisation as data: one file per language, a fixed set of snake_case keys with _text and _tooltip suffixes, editable in a live inspector. Maps onto zones-as-data for names and tooltips.
Game rules that are hard to tie to data (job ranges, baby-job lookup) are kept as small Lua predicates with named constants instead of hard-coded branches. Good for progression tiers.
Fallback 'missing' placeholders for models, sprites and textures, so content gaps stay visible rather than crashing. A useful debug habit for zone and loot data.

Real-time lighting with drop shadows is the headline visual claim (README.md line 10). Shader passes for directional and point-light shadows and a bindless entity picker live under korangar/shaders/. Category-level only: shadow map style and entity picking, not any copyrighted look.

briefs.label: Ground-marker glyph set (our own pictograms)
briefs.why: A row of tiny flat pictograms over the ground tells the player what is there (spawn, chest, shrine, sound source) before anything else. At 64 px and 375 wide it stays a readable blob, not a sprite fight.
briefs.keep: one flat glyph per category; sits on the ground as a small badge; drawn as a signed-distance icon so it stays crisp
briefs.change: our own pictogram shapes (not the donor's), a palette of our hue ramp, a different frame (ring or diamond, not the donor's badge)
briefs.ref: korangar/archive/data/texture/marker_light.png, marker_sound.png, marker_effect.png (64x64 IHDR; content not viewed)

briefs.label: Crisp SDF HUD glyph (eye and arrow family)
briefs.why: A two-state glyph (open eye and closed eye, expanded and collapsed arrows) makes a toggle readable at a glance on a phone, and the distance-field approach keeps it sharp at any size.
briefs.keep: two-state toggle glyphs as a pair; 32 px interface size; distance-field edge for crisp scaling
briefs.change: our own silhouette for the toggle (not an eye), different state cue (fill plus tilt, not open/closed), tuned for thumb-size hit areas

briefs.label: Walk-path chevron set
briefs.why: Three directional chevrons (straight, diagonal, goal) tell the player the next step on a route without a line that clutters the camera view.
briefs.keep: a small directional chevron set; straight, diagonal and goal states as one family
briefs.change: a goal state with a distinct shape (not a plain end-dot), a colour that matches our zone palette, chevrons that pulse only when the route changes

briefs.label: Per-job ID range predicate in Lua
briefs.why: A single function that answers 'is this a baby tier job' from ID ranges keeps the tier logic in one readable place and lets a data author extend it without rebuilding the client.
briefs.keep: one predicate per tier with nil-safe fallbacks; tier as a range of IDs; editable as data
briefs.change: we use named tiers in zone or progression data (not job IDs), and no copied range numbers; our own tier names and rules

briefs.label: Missing-asset placeholder model
briefs.why: A plain placeholder model shown when content is missing keeps gaps visible in play and in review, which speeds up content checks.
briefs.keep: obviously-wrong placeholder shape; used for any missing model, sprite or texture
briefs.change: our placeholder is a clear debug cube with a label, not a generic mesh; coloured by missing-kind
